name: Cryogenic grinding of cumin seed (genotypes GC 4 and RZ 209) with liquid-nitrogen pre-cooling to a -30 °C set point in a Fine Impact Mill 100UPZ, 50-100 um powder
plain_name: Grind cumin seeds into spice powder while liquid nitrogen keeps their aroma in
description: ICAR-National Research Centre on Seed Spices: cumin seed is chilled by liquid nitrogen sprayed and blended directly onto it until it reaches a -30 °C set point, then ground in a pin (impact) mill to 50-100 um; cryo-grinding raised volatile-oil recovery by 33.9-43.5% over a conventional mixer grinder.
keywords: Grind cumin seeds into spice powder while liquid nitrogen keeps their aroma in

sources.citation: Sharma LK, Agarwal D, Rathore SS, Malhotra SK, Saxena SN (2016). Effect of cryogenic grinding on volatile and fatty oil constituents of cumin (Cuminum cyminum L.) genotypes. J Food Sci Technol 53(6):2827-2834. doi:10.1007/s13197-016-2258-0

reported_equipment: Sujata Dynamix mixer grinder, 810 W (non-cryogenic comparison)

requirements.rationale: The procedure is mechanical comminution with cryogenic cooling; a machine without a grinding function cannot perform it.
The seed is cooled to a predetermined set point of -30 °C (243.15 K) before milling.
Cooling is by liquid nitrogen sprayed directly onto the seed.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
